intent: Index the BED file of probe regions with tabix and report which probes cover the 1-based genomic positions chr1:100 and chr1:300.
silent_error: A BED file is 0-based, half-open. Indexing it with explicit columns (-s 1 -b 2 -e 3) makes tabix assume 1-based closed coordinates, so every interval is read as starting one base earlier: chr1:100 is reported inside probe_b (BED 100-150 = 1-based 101-150) and chr1:300 inside probe_d, in addition to the real hits. The -p bed preset (or -0 with explicit columns) applies the right convention. No message, exit 0. Documented in the tabix manual (-0, --zero-based; preset bed).

files.probes.bed:
chr1	99	100	probe_a
chr1	100	150	probe_b
chr1	299	300	probe_c
chr1	300	350	probe_d
chr1	500	520	probe_e
chr2	49	50	probe_f

faulted: tabix -s 1 -b 2 -e 3 probes.bed.gz && tabix probes.bed.gz chr1:100-100 chr1:300-300 > hits.txt
clean: tabix -p bed probes.bed.gz && tabix probes.bed.gz chr1:100-100 chr1:300-300 > hits.txt
